name: Ratings (Dev)
description: Professional rating system for Jellyfin. Rate media with 1-10 stars, view detailed user ratings on hover, and see rating badges on media cards. Optimized for large libraries with lazy loading.
overview: Comprehensive rating plugin with star-based UI, average ratings display, detailed user rating popups, and performance-optimized card overlays for large media libraries.

versions.changelog: A security pass over the whole plugin. No exploitable weakness was found, and three smaller things were tightened. Profile header uploads now check that the file really is a GIF, MP4 or WEBM instead of believing the file name - the address that serves them is public by design, so it should not be possible to park arbitrary content there. Screenshots on a bug report are now fetched with the access token in a header rather than in the web address, keeping it out of browser history. And asking for better quality now respects each account's library access, so the reply cannot confirm the name of something in a library you are not allowed to browse.

Closes the last translation gaps, found by opening the app in French rather than by scanning for them: the Bio label, the header background hint, the TMDB catalog hint, and the "Current: GIF set" line. Cancel is also translated everywhere now - it had a key, but that key existed only in English and in none of the fifteen packs, so every language fell back to the English word.

Finishes the translation work. An audit of the whole plugin found another 141 phrases written straight into the markup - the profile settings window, the rating box, review comments, the media picker and its sort menu, friend menus, the join-watch window, chat controls, moderator and ban dialogs, and every "nothing here yet" message. All of them now go through the translation layer, with 119 new entries filled in for all fifteen languages. Each language pack now carries around 560 phrases, up from about 348 before this work started. Only six things stay in English on purpose: the Aurora, Sunset, Emerald and Minimal background names, and IMDb.

Finishes translating the profile. The previous release covered the tabs, buttons and the rating widget; this one covers the column beside them - Stats, Films, Shows, Hours, Avg, Ratings, Taste, Similar Taste, Activity, Add a film, the section headings, Back and Settings, Member since, and the "not on server" badge. Another seventeen labels, filled in for all fifteen languages. The online badge on the profile header now reads as words in your language rather than a raw status value.

The profile page, the friends panel and the star rating widget are translated at last. Those three areas were never connected to the translation system - the words were written straight into the markup - so they stayed in English no matter which language you picked, in all sixteen languages. Thirty labels now go through the translation layer and are filled in for every language, together with the thirty-eight strings added with the quality-request and bug-report queues. Every language pack gains sixty-eight entries. Thanks to chosqui for reporting it in discussion #76, with a Spanish patch that showed exactly what was missing.

Fixes the Quality and Bug Reports tabs never appearing in the Request Media window. That window is built in two places in the client and only one of them was given the new tabs - the one that was missed is the one that actually runs, so the two queues had no way in at all. Both now show the same five tabs.

Fixes the two support windows opening behind the Request Media window. Clicking a row under Quality looked as though nothing happened at all - the detail dialog was opening, just underneath the window it was launched from. Bug reports had the same problem, only visible enough through the dimmed background to notice. Both now open on top. Reporters can also see what happened to a bug report: the dialog lists your own reports underneath the box with their status and any reply from an admin, and sending one no longer closes the window, so the report lands in that list in front of you instead of vanishing.

Two new ways for people to tell you something is wrong, and one place to work through both. A Better Quality tab on the profile searches what is already on the server, and every result carries a button to say what is wrong with the current copy - blurry, wrong audio, missing subtitles. A Report a problem button next to Edit Profile takes a description plus screenshots, pasted straight from the clipboard or picked from disk. Both land in the Request Media modal as their own tabs, badged with how many are still open, where you can read the report, look at the screenshots, reply to the person who sent it, and mark it solved or declined - the reply is shown back to them. Also fixes a profile that read 0 films and 0 hours beside a taste chart reporting hundreds: those stats were derived from ratings alone, so anyone who watches without rating saw zeros. They now count what you have watched as well as what you have rated. And the genre breakdown endpoint was the one profile endpoint missing its visibility check, so a private profile's viewing habits could be read directly.

The admin request list now lays out properly on a phone. Each request kept its title, user, date and status on one row, so on a narrow screen the title was squeezed down to a few characters, and the media-link and rejection-reason boxes were split across a width that could not hold them. The title now takes a line of its own with the details underneath it, the expand arrow sits at the right edge, and the two input boxes stack at full width. Reported and written by @daki456 (PR #78). The category list also gets the same 500 pixel scroll height as the production build, which had drifted apart from it.

Leftover trickplay cleanup now covers both ways Jellyfin stores it. Libraries set to 'save trickplay images next to media' keep the tiles in a folder beside each video instead of the central directory, and those were invisible to the previous scan - a server using that setting looked as though it had no trickplay at all. Both places are now scanned and cleaned, and the panel reports what it found in each.

Fixes the leftover-trickplay scan looking in the wrong place, which is why it reported nothing to clean up. Jellyfin stores trickplay in folders grouped by the first two characters of each item id, and the scan was treating one of those groups as the whole directory - so it only ever looked at a single group out of 256, and usually an empty one. It now reads the real directory and looks inside every group, and the panel names the directory it checked so the result can be trusted.

Fixes the leftover-trickplay panel showing the words orphanTitle and orphanNone instead of readable text, and makes its result verifiable. It now says how many trickplay folders it examined and where, so 'nothing to clean up' can be told apart from a scan that never ran. If there are no trickplay folders at all yet, it says that explicitly.

Two clean-ups from the security review. Searching and browsing through the plugin now respects the libraries each account is allowed to see, so a user with limited access can no longer come across titles from libraries they cannot open - this affected the plugin's own search, the sorted library view and the latest-media list. And when the plugin refuses an action because you are not an administrator, it now says so properly instead of returning a server error; access was already correctly denied, but the message was wrong.

Adds leftover trickplay cleanup to Media Management. Deleting media leaves its trickplay tiles on disk, and on a large library that can add up to a great deal of space. Clearing the whole trickplay folder would recover it but forces every remaining file to be reprocessed, which can take days. The Disk Usage tab now lists only the folders belonging to media that is no longer in your library, shows how much space they take, and can remove them - nothing you still have is touched and nothing is reprocessed. Administrators only. Also gives the Reviews tab a proper card with the poster, the year and a Movie or Series badge instead of a plain row of text, and fixes a broken confirmation message when saving privacy settings.

Security release. Fixes three ways a user could have got script to run inside someone else's session: one through a profile's favourite films, which affected anyone viewing that profile, and two through links attached to media and deletion requests, which ran in an administrator's session and so could have been used to act as an administrator. The underlying cause was that the routine used to make text safe for display did not escape quotation marks, which is what let a crafted value break out. Also closes several privacy and permission gaps: private profiles could be read through the newer profile endpoints, a private list could be read by copying it, direct messages ignored blocking, the recent-requests list showed every user's requests to non-administrators, and a user banned from playback or over their quota could bypass both by sending their login token in a different but equally valid form. Nothing in the interface changes.

Search now ignores punctuation and spacing, so 'xfiles', 'x files' and 'X-Files' all find the same show - the same goes for 'spiderman', 'walle' or 'swat'. It applies to the film search on your profile, the media picker and the Media Management search box. Jellyfin's own search is still tried first; the looser match only steps in when that finds nothing. Also completes an authentication clean-up: seventeen more endpoints identified the caller in a stricter way than the rest of the plugin, so apps that sign in with a plain token - TV and mobile clients in particular - were refused by them even though the same token worked elsewhere. Every endpoint in the plugin now identifies you the same way. Nothing changes for the web interface, which was never affected.

Fixes removing a rating failing with 'Could not remove that rating'. The delete request was rejected before it did anything: that endpoint only recognised one of the ways a client can present its login, and the Remove button uses the other. It now identifies you the same way the rest of the plugin does. Saving a rating went through the same check and is fixed with it. Also makes the edit and remove buttons easy to press: the card grew slightly on hover at the same moment the buttons appeared, so the button moved out from under the pointer as you reached for it. Cards no longer resize, the buttons are larger, and they stay visible on phones and TVs where there is no hover at all.

Four requested additions. Ratings can now be edited or removed directly from the Ratings tab, including titles that are not on the server - previously the only way to change one of those was to add the film to a profile row and rate it again. Reviews can now be written for catalog titles too, in the same box as the rating. Custom profile rows can be reordered with arrows in the row header. And a rating can now be agreed or disagreed with even when the person did not write a review; your own vote is remembered and shown when you come back.

Removes the empty gap under the header on phones. The plugin used to place its buttons in a full-width row below the header and pushed the whole page down to make room. The buttons now collapse behind the dropdown, but the space was still being reserved, leaving a blank strip above Home and Favourites. The space is now only reserved while the menu is actually open. Fixes the plugin's buttons staying on top of the video player, which in portrait covered the controls needed to get out of a video (issue #74). Recent Activity now shows the poster for titles that are not on the server; the rating showed but the artwork was blank, because it was being requested from your server for a title that only exists in the catalog.

The ElegantFin layout fix added in the previous release now applies only to servers actually using that skin. It adjusts two of Jellyfin's own elements to stop the plugin's buttons being cut off on phones, so leaving it switched on everywhere was heavier-handed than needed. The plugin now checks whether the skin is loaded - pasted into Custom CSS, added as an @import, or linked as a stylesheet - and applies the adjustment only then. Every other theme is left completely untouched.

Media Management now shows a TMDB poster for titles Jellyfin has no artwork for. An item Jellyfin never identified keeps the raw '[tt...]' from its filename and has no images at all, so those rows drew a grey box. The IMDB id is taken from the item, or read out of its name when Jellyfin never matched it, and the cover is fetched from TMDB in the background - the list itself is never held up, so the poster appears on the next load. Needs the TMDB token already used for catalog search, and can be turned off in settings. Also applies mobile dropdown feedback from discussion #71: the menu now lays out as a wrapping row of icons instead of one full-width row per button, which on a phone left most buttons unreachable behind the tab bar, plus the reporter's fix for buttons being cut off under themed skins such as ElegantFin.

Fixes Media Management showing no posters, no media type, and dashes instead of rating, plays, size and deletion status on every tab. An earlier update renamed the fields in the plugin's API responses to start with a lower-case letter, but parts of the interface still looked for the old capitalised names and so found nothing. Titles and years kept working because they had already been updated, which is why the tables looked half-filled. Media Management now reads every field correctly, and the same fix is applied to the Scheduled tab, the 'Leaving in' badges on cards and detail pages, and the media request and ban screens, which were affected in the same way.

Fixes titles that are not on the server staying invisible in your profile rows until you added another item. The row was drawn by counting only the entries that point at a file on the server, and then drawing that many cards - so a catalog title, which has no server file by design, was never reached. Adding another item redrew the row using a different rule that counted it correctly, which is why it suddenly appeared. Both the first draw and the redraw now use one shared rule, so a row containing only catalog titles displays them immediately.

Fixes titles that are not on the server disappearing from your profile rows. Adding one worked and it was saved correctly, but reopening the profile ran a clean-up step that kept only the item id, title and poster and then discarded anything without an item id - which is exactly what a catalog title is. The card vanished, and the next save wrote the shortened row back, deleting it on the server for good. Catalog titles now keep all their details and survive reopening the profile. Rows saved before this update that already lost their titles cannot be recovered and need re-adding.

Fixes adding a title from the catalog to a favourites row doing nothing for some media, and those same titles refusing to drag. The Add button and the drag handler both received the film's details as text embedded in the page, and an apostrophe in the title cut that text short - so the browser threw a syntax error and neither action ever ran. 'Schindler's List' and 'Ocean's Eleven' failed while 'Blade Runner (1982)' worked, which is why it looked random. Titles are now encoded so any character is safe. The same flaw is fixed for the message button on usernames containing an apostrophe, and for the genre picker.

Fixes rating a film that is not on the server failing with a not-authenticated error. Four endpoints checked the signed-in user in a stricter way than the rest of the plugin and rejected perfectly valid requests - rating a TMDB title, reading your own rating for an item, the batch rating lookup used to draw badges, and listing or creating media requests. They now identify you the same way every other endpoint does, so any client sending a valid token is accepted.

Fixes new media being announced but never appearing in the Latest Media list. The list was ordered by the date Jellyfin takes from the file itself, not by when the media actually reached your server - so anything copied in keeping its original timestamps sorted to wherever that old date fell, usually past the end of the list. You would get the 'now available' notification and then find nothing there. The list now also includes everything the plugin announced, dated by when it actually saw it, so the notification and the list can no longer disagree. Items removed from the server since being announced are left out.

Further hardening of the watching hover card, following up the security fix in the previous version. The card no longer reads any text back out of the page at all - the title it shows while loading now comes from data the plugin already holds. Re-inserting text taken from the page undoes whatever escaping made it safe, so the read was removed rather than escaped. Numbers shown on the card (year, running time, score) are also validated as numbers before being displayed, which additionally stops an unexpected value breaking the card.

Security fix. The hover card that shows what someone is watching built an image tag by pasting an item id straight into HTML, and that id was read back out of the page. A crafted value could have escaped the image tag and run script for another user viewing the profile. Item ids are now rejected unless they are genuine Jellyfin ids, and the image is created as a real element instead of being assembled from text. Reported by GitHub CodeQL (js/xss-through-dom, high severity).

API fixes for third-party and TV clients. Social endpoints previously accepted only the raw X-Emby-Token header, so any app using Jellyfin's standard authentication got 401 from every social call while the identical request worked against the ratings API - they now accept every form Jellyfin does, including API keys. All responses are also camelCase now; some endpoints returned PascalCase and others camelCase, which silently produced empty fields in other clients. Existing data files still load correctly. New endpoints make a profile page far cheaper to build: one aggregated profile call instead of nine, ratings/reviews/activity that already include title, poster and year, a per-user rating histogram, a capability check, and paging on followers and following.

Hover what someone is watching to see the poster and details. Pointing at the title in the Similar Taste list now brings up a card with the artwork, year, running time, age rating, community score, genres and a synopsis - so you can tell what it is without leaving the profile. For an episode it shows the series artwork and the episode name. Details are fetched once and remembered for the rest of the session.

Live presence, full titles, and a Watch too button. The Similar Taste list now updates by itself when someone comes online or starts watching - you no longer have to close and reopen the profile to see it. What someone is watching moved onto its own line, so long series titles are readable in full instead of being squeezed between the name and the match percentage. And each person who is watching now has a Watch too button: press it and you are asked whether to join them at the point they are at right now, or start from the beginning.

See who is online and what they are watching, and a much better looking profile name. The Similar Taste list now shows a dot on each person: bright green and pulsing means they are watching something right now, and the card shows what it is with a clock that ticks along live; soft green means online but not watching; grey means offline. The profile name has also been fixed - it was drawn as a colour gradient clipped to the letters, which over a photo or video header turned it into washed-out grey. It is now solid white with proper display typography, using each platform's large-text typeface.

Back now returns to the previous profile instead of closing everything. Opening someone's profile from a followers, following or Similar Taste list used to be a one-way trip - pressing Back tore the whole profile window down and dropped you back on the page behind it. It now steps back through the profiles you visited, and only closes once there is nowhere left to go back to. The button reads 'Back to profile' when there is.

The Similar Taste list now includes everyone on the server. Users with a private profile were previously left out of the matching, which made the list thin on servers where people had tightened their privacy settings. Since what the card shows is an aggregate genre percentage rather than any particular title, everyone is now included. Blocked users are still left out, in both directions.

See what you actually watch, and find people who watch the same things. Profiles now have a Taste ring in the sidebar showing your genre breakdown by real watch time - taken from what you have actually played, not just what you rated - with hours watched and a percentage for each genre. Below it, a Similar Taste list ranks other users by how closely their genre mix matches yours, showing the genres you have most in common. Click anyone to open their profile, or use the envelope button to send them a private message straight away. Private profiles and blocked users are left out of the match list.

Rate films that are not on the server, keep ratings readable after media is deleted, choose your TMDB search language, and browse other users. You can now rate a title added to a profile row from the catalog even though it is not on the server - hover it and press Rate. If it is added to the library later, your rating attaches to it automatically. Ratings also remember the title, year and poster of what you rated, so deleting a film no longer leaves a nameless row of stars behind; older ratings fill this in as you use them. Admins can set the language TMDB search returns titles in (Settings, TMDB Search Language) instead of always getting English. And profiles have a new Other Users tab listing everyone on the server, with a filter box, so you can find and visit other people's profiles without knowing their name in advance.

Header buttons now fold into a dropdown menu on phones. With search, language, profile, requests, notifications, latest media, chat and friends all in the header there was simply not enough room on a small screen, and buttons ended up clipped or wrapping badly. On phone-sized screens they now sit behind a single arrow button and open as a tidy list, with the search box at full width. Unread chat messages light a dot on that button so you can still tell something is waiting inside. Nothing changes on tablets or desktop. Thanks to @chosqui for the suggestion (discussion #71).

Fixes from reported issues. The Save button in Profile Settings now works - it was calling an address the server does not accept, so nothing was ever saved, and the privacy tick-boxes always looked switched on regardless of your real settings (#72). The search bar no longer disappears on phones held in portrait: it now shrinks to just the magnifier icon and expands when tapped, instead of being hidden below 400px wide (#69). Deleting media now also removes its trickplay thumbnails and any extracted subtitles or attachments, which used to be left behind forever (#70). Uninstalling the plugin now really removes the header buttons - the plugin no longer edits Jellyfin's index.html, and it cleans up that edit if an older version made it, so users no longer have to clear their browser cache by hand (#66). When an old plugin folder cannot be deleted on Windows because the file is locked, its meta.json is now removed so the stale version stops being listed and loaded (#67). New-media notifications now log exactly why an item was treated as new, to make the remaining reports diagnosable (#65).

Downloads get dramatically smaller and the server writes to disk far less. The plugin's script, stylesheet and language files are now sent pre-compressed, so a first page load transfers about 108 KB instead of 676 KB - roughly six times less. This works even if you reach Jellyfin over HTTPS directly, where Jellyfin's own compression is switched off by default. Separately, rapid saves are now merged into one write: previously every user's presence heartbeat rewrote the entire online-users file, so a handful of people online meant constant disk churn. Nothing is lost - pending saves are flushed on shutdown and before any backup export or import. Also adds automated build checks so a release can no longer go out with an unminified or syntactically broken script.

Big speed and smoothness pass. Pages load a lot lighter: the plugin's styles are now a proper stylesheet instead of being stuffed inside the script, and only your own language is downloaded rather than all sixteen - together that roughly halves what your browser has to fetch and parse on every page. Scrolling through libraries is noticeably smoother because the plugin no longer re-scans the whole page every time anything on it changes. The admin Media list now asks the database for just the page you're looking at instead of loading your entire library first, so it opens quickly even on large collections. Chat only fetches new messages instead of re-downloading the last 50 every two seconds, and background tabs stop polling entirely. Watching something no longer rewrites a settings file on every few seconds of playback. Data files are also written more safely, so a crash or power cut mid-save can no longer leave them corrupted. Includes the admin category list scrollbar fix from PR #73.

Fixes the 'new media' pop-ups that kept appearing for films and shows that were already on your server. The plugin now learns your existing library the first time it runs and only alerts you about genuinely new additions. A library scan, a re-scan, or installing the plugin on a big existing collection no longer floods you with 'now available' alerts for old content - including whole seasons that were already there.

Compatibility fix and ratings now visible to other apps. Fixed the Friends panel ('Online' tab, friend search) and live chat throwing errors on newer Jellyfin (10.11.10/11) - they work again. Your ratings are now also saved into Jellyfin's own rating field, so other apps and tools (like Maintainerr) can read them through the Jellyfin API. There's a new one-time button in the plugin settings to sync all your existing ratings across, plus an optional setting to also write the average into each item's Community Rating.

Profile drag-and-drop and search popups. Fixed dragging a poster from Recent Activity into a favorite row (it now sticks). You can also drag films/shows straight from the 'Add a film' search results into a row - including titles that aren't on the server yet. And every search result now shows a hover popup with the full title, year and description, so you can tell them apart at a glance.

Profile polish. Hover any favorite poster to see a popup with the full title, year and description (so you can recognise titles without opening them). Fixed the profile header: when you set a GIF/video background, your name and details no longer look greyed out - they stay bright and readable over the video.

Profile additions and two fixes. You can now add films/shows that are NOT yet on the server to your profile rows - hover one to reveal a Request button, or click it for a reminder to request it. Edit Profile now lets you upload your own looping GIF or video to show behind your name and picture. Fixes: the rating number no longer lingers on a star after you stop hovering, and deleting a duplicate now actually removes the file so it no longer comes back after a library scan.

Faster Latest Media and a couple of nice touches. Reworked the recent-media lookups so the 'Latest Media' panel and browsing load quicker on large libraries. When you hover the rating stars, the number now appears inside the star you're pointing at, with a small pop animation. Added an admin option to show or hide the rating badge on poster cards - turning it off (or turning ratings off) now removes the badges right away instead of leaving old ones behind.

Speed and reliability improvements. Made the 'Latest Media' panel and general browsing noticeably faster on large libraries by removing heavy background work that ran every minute. Fixed old movies and shows sometimes appearing as 'newly added' when they were not - now only genuinely new media triggers a notification, and the same item is never announced twice (even after a server restart). Fixed custom sorting showing no cards when several folders are combined into one library view.

Fixed the Duplicates tool wrongly flagging whole TV shows as duplicates. It was treating every episode of a series as a copy of the same thing (e.g. 705 'copies' of The Simpsons). Now it only groups true duplicates - the same episode (or movie) appearing more than once - so different episodes are no longer shown as duplicates.
Faster loading. The plugin's add-on is now packaged more compactly (about a third smaller), so it downloads and starts a bit quicker. No features change.

Faster page loads. The plugin's add-on now loads from your browser's cache instead of downloading again every time you open a page, so your library opens quicker after the first visit. Nothing else changes.
Security: removed the unused standalone profile page that triggered several CodeQL warnings. The in-app profile and everything else are unchanged.

Real fix for favorites not saving: the profile loads favorites from the server's PascalCase JSON, but the UI read camelCase, so rows loaded EMPTY and the next save overwrote the saved items. Favorites are now normalized on load. Also added a reliable drop zone so you can drag a poster from Recent Activity onto a row (including the + slot).

Favorites finally save reliably (removed a save-success snapshot overwrite that dropped items added while a save was in flight). Drag-to-reorder and add/remove now update only the affected row instead of reloading the whole profile, and you can drag a poster from Recent Activity straight into a favorites row.

Fixed favorites not saving (debounced saves prevent a clobber race that wiped items); favorite-row posters now load from the current server address (fixes blank posters via reverse proxy/domain); fixed the profile Like 404 (wrong route); added the plugin version to the dashboard header.

Profile stats now count rated films/shows (was 0). Dashboard: added Revision History and fixed list number alignment. Media picker: added 'Show all (random)' so you can add any media to rows, not just rated. Added favorites-save diagnostics to track down the not-saving issue.

Faster profile load (Stats no longer runs a query per series - was the main ~5s cause). Add-to-row chooser now shows real row names. Removed the confusing Lists tab/stat/sidebar. Favorites save now surfaces errors instead of failing silently.

Media picker now respects the category tab (Movies/Series/etc.) when sorting by My Ratings - no longer always shows movies. Favorite rows scroll with transparent hover arrows instead of a scrollbar. Replaced mirror reflections with clean drop shadows. Faster profile load: the overview now fetches ratings once and reuses them across distribution/posters/reviews/activity.

Add-a-film now searches the full external catalog via TMDB (paste a free TMDB Read Access Token in plugin settings) - results not on your server can be requested in one click; server results get a '+ Add' button to add to a chosen favorites row (or a new row). Drag-and-drop to reorder films within a favorites row. Fixed the Lists 404 (wrong route) so the Lists count works. Fixed a broken favorites remove button.

Profile bug fixes: much faster load (single batched library query instead of hundreds of per-item lookups), Reviews count now calculated, you show as Online on your own profile, live WebSocket online-status updates (no reopen needed), the three-dot menu popup positioned correctly, and review like/dislike buttons now work.

Profile polish: lock background-page scrolling while the profile is open (no more scroll bleed), plus a big visual upgrade - poster mirror reflections, glassmorphism side panels, glowing stars/accents, gradient avatar/title, smoother hover/press animations, and a background picker (Aurora/Sunset/Emerald/Minimal, remembered per browser). Note: full IMDb-style external catalog search is coming next and will need a free TMDB API key.

Profile redesign: new two-column Letterboxd-style Overview with a right sidebar (Add-a-film search/request, stats, ratings histogram, lists, activity), real poster strip and recent reviews, an 'Add a film' box that searches your server (click to watch) or requests missing titles by name/IMDb, plus hover/press animations and a success toast.

Profile page: fix media names showing 'Unknown' in Ratings/Reviews/Activity (server now resolves item name/year/library status), star ratings now show an exact-value tooltip (e.g. 8/10 · 4/5), media cards/titles are clickable to open the item, and the header profile button moved next to the language button. Also adds clear startup logging for the duplicate-folder cleanup.

Fix duplicate plugin installs: on startup the plugin now removes older versioned folders that share its GUID (keeps only the running version), ending the 'two versions installed / restart required' loop. GUID-scoped and strictly-older-only, so it never affects other plugins or the current version.

Performance: cache the 1.6MB ratings.js in-memory with ETag revalidation (browsers get a tiny 304 instead of re-downloading on every load/restart), load the 17 persisted data files in parallel at startup to cut boot/first-use latency, and remove a duplicate WebSocket service registration. No feature/data changes.

Fix: My Rating library sort - render sorted results into a plugin-owned grid (no longer fights Jellyfin's view, fixes page 2/3 jumping back to page 1), unified API auth so SortedLibrary accepts X-Emby-Token (fixes empty/no-items results), clearer empty-state messages
Fix: 401 Unauthorized error - API now accepts X-Emby-Token header properly
Fix: My Ratings sorting now works - shows your rated items sorted by rating, default shows random
Media picker: Sort options (My Ratings, Community Rating, Newest, Name), rating badges visible on cards
Fix: Ratings/reviews/activity tabs now load correctly on profile
Profile: Add row with title picker, 30 items per row, lazy loading, fixed following count stats
Profile: Multiple favorite rows (up to 5), library browser with categories, pagination, sorting by ratings
New: Favorite films with media picker, profile button toggle in settings
New: Profile button in header bar to access your profile
Fix: Profile stats layout, fullscreen toggle, settings modal, rating distribution, activity feed
New: Letterboxd-style profile modal with tabs, stats, follows, likes, lists
Fix: Profile links now navigate to full Letterboxd-style profile page
New: Letterboxd-style user profiles with custom lists, follows, profile likes, stats, and full customization
Security: Fix remaining CodeQL vulnerabilities (URL whitelist, XSS)
Fix: Moderator panel user colors now load correctly (userId format normalization)
Fix: Moderator panel now correctly displays saved user style colors
Security fixes, moderator panel colors persist, dashboard requests open modal
Settings: Masonry column layout - groups flow to fill gaps properly (3 cols wide, 2 cols medium, 1 col small)
Dashboard: All elements clickable (rating distribution modal, user profiles, requests). Settings: Improved full-width 2-3 column layout
Dashboard: 5 sections (activity, top rated, active users, rating distribution, requests). Settings: full-width layout for wide screens
